heading: INT. HOLLOWAY HOUSE - DRAWING ROOM - LATE AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. HOLLOWAY HOUSE - DRAWING ROOM - LATE AFTERNOON
Rain has been falling since the cemetery and now it ticks against the tall windows like something asking to be let in.
Lamps are lit too early.
The room smells of lilies, wet wool and the kind of coffee that is made in urns.

ODILE VANCE, sixty, stands by the sideboard with a plate she will never finish, and she watches her late husband's brother HARLAN pour himself a third whisky with a steadiness that is almost an accusation.
Across the room, PRU, the dead man's daughter, folds and unfolds a funeral program until it has no shape, while TEODOR, the family lawyer, drifts behind her saying nothing in a very organised way.

Near the piano, ROWAN, the dead man's nurse, who is wearing a borrowed black cardigan and who uses they and them, stands alone with their hands in their pockets, and they are the only one in the room who has noticed the study door is open.
You told the police you were in Dover that night.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: I told them what was true, Odile.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: The landline in the hall RINGS.
Nobody moves.
It rings again.
I'll go.
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: He goes.
His voice carries back, flat and polite, through the open door.
Holloway residence. ... No, he is not available. ... Who is this, please?
units.name: TEODOR

units.text: Rowan turns toward the sound.
Pru stops folding.
Who is it?
units.name: PRU

units.text: Say that again.
units.name: TEODOR
paren: a long pause, then no longer polite

units.text: Harlan sets down the glass.
The lilies shiver in a draught from the study.
Rowan takes one step toward the hall, and Odile, without turning her head, says their name like a warning.
Rowan.
units.name: ODILE
